decisions.reason: The indoor air quality module is a current-generation sensing building block with lasting demand from schools and building automation, so its results likely meet the aspiration and dropping it would gain little.
As the current generation of a basic measurement module that replaced version 2.0, it is a core catalogue item with low carrying cost and no evident shortfall.
The MQTT proxy adds IoT value across all modules at low maintenance cost, so it is kept even though the firm may later fold its function into other bindings.
Demand for CO2 monitoring rose sharply with ventilation concerns, so this module likely exceeds the aspiration and fits the sensing strategy.

The touch panel accessory is a peripheral item with less certain results, but it costs little to carry, so the firm's slack allows keeping it, with a somewhat higher risk of withdrawal during component shortages.
